# Requirement
```text
Airlines offer different flights. Each flight has its unique id. A flight is open for booking and closed by order of the company. A customer can book one or more flights, for different passengers. A reservation concerns a single flight and a single passenger, has a unique id. A reservation can be confirmed or canceled. A flight has a departure airport and an arrival airport. Each airport has its unique id. A flight has a day and time of departure, and a day and time of arrival (e.g. 2024-12-08 13:00:00). A flight may include stopovers in one or more airport(s). A stopover has a departure time and an arrival time. Each airport serves one or more cities.
Functional requirement:
1.Publish a flight for booking. An airline can publish a newly created flight to make it available for customer bookings. The system first confirms that the flight has valid departure and arrival timestamps in yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss format, then checks temporal consistency — currentTime < departureTime < arrivalTime — and route integrity — departureAirport ≠ arrivalAirport. A flight may be published only once, and before publishing, the flight's openForBooking status must be false. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
2.Create a booking for passengers on a flight. A customer selects a specific open flight and supplies a list of passengers names. The system checks that there are no duplicate passengers on the flight and the current time is before the flight departure time. It then generates a booking for the customer and creates a reservation with a unique ID for each passenger in that booking. Each reservation is initially placed in "pending" status until the customer confirms it. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
3.Confirm or cancel an existing reservation in a booking. The system checks that the flight has not yet departed and is still open for booking. The customer can then confirm or cancel a reservation by providing its reservation ID. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
4.Close an open flight. An airline can close an existing flight that has not yet departed. The system verifies that the flight is currently open; if so, it changes the status to closed and cancels every confirmed reservation. Closing is not allowed on the same calendar day as the flight's departure — even if the current time is before the departure time. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
5.Retrieve all confirmed reservations for a specific flight. Given a flight object, the system retrieves every confirmed reservation on that flight, provided the flight is currently open for booking. It returns a list of reservations, or empty list if none exist.
```

```plantuml
@startuml

title flights Model

class Airline {
    flights : List<Flight>
    addFlight(f : Flight) : void
    closeFlight(flightId : String, now : EDate) : boolean
    publishFlight(f : Flight, now : EDate) : boolean
    removeFlight(f : Flight) : void
    searchFlights(origin : String, dest : String, date : EDate) : List<Flight>
}
class Airport {
    id : String
    servesForCities : List<City>
    addCity(c : City) : void
}
class Booking {
    customer : Customer
    reservations : List<Reservation>
    createReservation(f : Flight, passenger : String, now : EDate) : boolean
}
class City {
}
class Customer {
    bookings : List<Booking>
    addBooking(f : Flight, now : EDate, listOfPassengerNames : List<String>) : boolean
    cancel(reservationID : String, now : EDate) : boolean
    confirm(reservationID : String, now : EDate) : boolean
}
class Flight {
    arrivalTime : EDate
    departureTime : EDate
    id : String
    openForBooking : boolean
    arrivalAirport : Airport
    departureAirport : Airport
    reservations : List<Reservation>
    stopovers : List<Stopover>
    addStopover(stop : Stopover, now : EDate) : boolean
    getConfirmedReservations() : List<Reservation>
    removeStopover(stop : Stopover, now : EDate) : boolean
}
class Passenger {
    name : String
}
class Reservation {
    id : String
    status : ReservationStatus
    flight : Flight
    passenger : Passenger
}
class Stopover {
    arrivalTime : EDate
    departureTime : EDate
    airport : Airport
}
enum ReservationStatus {
    PENDING
    CONFIRMED
    CANCELED
}

Airline *-- "*" Flight : flights
Airport --> "*" City : servesForCities
Booking --> Customer : customer
Booking *-- "*" Reservation : reservations
Customer --> "*" Booking : bookings
Flight --> Airport : arrivalAirport
Flight --> Airport : departureAirport
Flight --> "*" Reservation : reservations
Flight *-- "*" Stopover : stopovers
Reservation --> Flight : flight
Reservation --> Passenger : passenger
Stopover --> Airport : airport
@enduml
```

# Requirement
```text
Airlines offer different flights. Each flight has its unique id. A flight is open for booking and closed by order of the company. A customer can book one or more flights, for different passengers. A reservation concerns a single flight and a single passenger, has a unique id. A reservation can be confirmed or canceled. A flight has a departure airport and an arrival airport. Each airport has its unique id. A flight has a day and time of departure, and a day and time of arrival (e.g. 2024-12-08 13:00:00). A flight may include stopovers in one or more airport(s). A stopover has a departure time and an arrival time. Each airport serves one or more cities.
Functional requirement:
1.Publish a flight for booking. An airline can publish a newly created flight to make it available for customer bookings. The system first confirms that the flight has valid departure and arrival timestamps in yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss format, then checks temporal consistency — currentTime < departureTime < arrivalTime — and route integrity — departureAirport ≠ arrivalAirport. A flight may be published only once, and before publishing, the flight's openForBooking status must be false. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
2.Create a booking for passengers on a flight. A customer selects a specific open flight and supplies a list of passengers names. The system checks that there are no duplicate passengers on the flight and the current time is before the flight departure time. It then generates a booking for the customer and creates a reservation with a unique ID for each passenger in that booking. Each reservation is initially placed in "pending" status until the customer confirms it. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
3.Confirm or cancel an existing reservation in a booking. The system checks that the flight has not yet departed and is still open for booking. The customer can then confirm or cancel a reservation by providing its reservation ID. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
4.Close an open flight. An airline can close an existing flight that has not yet departed. The system verifies that the flight is currently open; if so, it changes the status to closed and cancels every confirmed reservation. Closing is not allowed on the same calendar day as the flight's departure — even if the current time is before the departure time. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
5.Retrieve all confirmed reservations for a specific flight. Given a flight object, the system retrieves every confirmed reservation on that flight, provided the flight is currently open for booking. It returns a list of reservations, or empty list if none exist.
```

# Requirement
```text
Airlines offer different flights. Each flight has its unique id. A flight is open for booking and closed by order of the company. A customer can book one or more flights, for different passengers. A reservation concerns a single flight and a single passenger, has a unique id. A reservation can be confirmed or canceled. A flight has a departure airport and an arrival airport. Each airport has its unique id. A flight has a day and time of departure, and a day and time of arrival (e.g. 2024-12-08 13:00:00). A flight may include stopovers in one or more airport(s). A stopover has a departure time and an arrival time. Each airport serves one or more cities.
Functional requirement:
1.Publish a flight for booking. An airline can publish a newly created flight to make it available for customer bookings. The system first confirms that the flight has valid departure and arrival timestamps in yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss format, then checks temporal consistency — currentTime < departureTime < arrivalTime — and route integrity — departureAirport ≠ arrivalAirport. A flight may be published only once, and before publishing, the flight's openForBooking status must be false. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
2.Create a booking for passengers on a flight. A customer selects a specific open flight and supplies a list of passengers names. The system checks that there are no duplicate passengers on the flight and the current time is before the flight departure time. It then generates a booking for the customer and creates a reservation with a unique ID for each passenger in that booking. Each reservation is initially placed in "pending" status until the customer confirms it. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
3.Confirm or cancel an existing reservation in a booking. The system checks that the flight has not yet departed and is still open for booking. The customer can then confirm or cancel a reservation by providing its reservation ID. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
4.Close an open flight. An airline can close an existing flight that has not yet departed. The system verifies that the flight is currently open; if so, it changes the status to closed and cancels every confirmed reservation. Closing is not allowed on the same calendar day as the flight's departure — even if the current time is before the departure time. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
5.Retrieve all confirmed reservations for a specific flight. Given a flight object, the system retrieves every confirmed reservation on that flight, provided the flight is currently open for booking. It returns a list of reservations, or empty list if none exist.
```

# Requirement
```text
Airlines offer different flights. Each flight has its unique id. A flight is open for booking and closed by order of the company. A customer can book one or more flights, for different passengers. A reservation concerns a single flight and a single passenger, has a unique id. A reservation can be confirmed or canceled. A flight has a departure airport and an arrival airport. Each airport has its unique id. A flight has a day and time of departure, and a day and time of arrival (e.g. 2024-12-08 13:00:00). A flight may include stopovers in one or more airport(s). A stopover has a departure time and an arrival time. Each airport serves one or more cities.
Functional requirement:
1.Publish a flight for booking. An airline can publish a newly created flight to make it available for customer bookings. The system first confirms that the flight has valid departure and arrival timestamps in yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss format, then checks temporal consistency — currentTime < departureTime < arrivalTime — and route integrity — departureAirport ≠ arrivalAirport. A flight may be published only once, and before publishing, the flight's openForBooking status must be false. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
2.Create a booking for passengers on a flight. A customer selects a specific open flight and supplies a list of passengers names. The system checks that there are no duplicate passengers on the flight and the current time is before the flight departure time. It then generates a booking for the customer and creates a reservation with a unique ID for each passenger in that booking. Each reservation is initially placed in "pending" status until the customer confirms it. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
3.Confirm or cancel an existing reservation in a booking. The system checks that the flight has not yet departed and is still open for booking. The customer can then confirm or cancel a reservation by providing its reservation ID. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
4.Close an open flight. An airline can close an existing flight that has not yet departed. The system verifies that the flight is currently open; if so, it changes the status to closed and cancels every confirmed reservation. Closing is not allowed on the same calendar day as the flight's departure — even if the current time is before the departure time. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
5.Retrieve all confirmed reservations for a specific flight. Given a flight object, the system retrieves every confirmed reservation on that flight, provided the flight is currently open for booking. It returns a list of reservations, or empty list if none exist.
```

# Requirement
```text
Airlines offer different flights. Each flight has its unique id. A flight is open for booking and closed by order of the company. A customer can book one or more flights, for different passengers. A reservation concerns a single flight and a single passenger, has a unique id. A reservation can be confirmed or canceled. A flight has a departure airport and an arrival airport. Each airport has its unique id. A flight has a day and time of departure, and a day and time of arrival (e.g. 2024-12-08 13:00:00). A flight may include stopovers in one or more airport(s). A stopover has a departure time and an arrival time. Each airport serves one or more cities.
Functional requirement:
1.Publish a flight for booking. An airline can publish a newly created flight to make it available for customer bookings. The system first confirms that the flight has valid departure and arrival timestamps in yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss format, then checks temporal consistency — currentTime < departureTime < arrivalTime — and route integrity — departureAirport ≠ arrivalAirport. A flight may be published only once, and before publishing, the flight's openForBooking status must be false. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
2.Create a booking for passengers on a flight. A customer selects a specific open flight and supplies a list of passengers names. The system checks that there are no duplicate passengers on the flight and the current time is before the flight departure time. It then generates a booking for the customer and creates a reservation with a unique ID for each passenger in that booking. Each reservation is initially placed in "pending" status until the customer confirms it. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
3.Confirm or cancel an existing reservation in a booking. The system checks that the flight has not yet departed and is still open for booking. The customer can then confirm or cancel a reservation by providing its reservation ID. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
4.Close an open flight. An airline can close an existing flight that has not yet departed. The system verifies that the flight is currently open; if so, it changes the status to closed and cancels every confirmed reservation. Closing is not allowed on the same calendar day as the flight's departure — even if the current time is before the departure time. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
5.Retrieve all confirmed reservations for a specific flight. Given a flight object, the system retrieves every confirmed reservation on that flight, provided the flight is currently open for booking. It returns a list of reservations, or empty list if none exist.
```

# Requirement
```text
Airlines offer different flights. Each flight has its unique id. A flight is open for booking and closed by order of the company. A customer can book one or more flights, for different passengers. A reservation concerns a single flight and a single passenger, has a unique id. A reservation can be confirmed or canceled. A flight has a departure airport and an arrival airport. Each airport has its unique id. A flight has a day and time of departure, and a day and time of arrival (e.g. 2024-12-08 13:00:00). A flight may include stopovers in one or more airport(s). A stopover has a departure time and an arrival time. Each airport serves one or more cities.
Functional requirement:
1.Publish a flight for booking. An airline can publish a newly created flight to make it available for customer bookings. The system first confirms that the flight has valid departure and arrival timestamps in yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss format, then checks temporal consistency — currentTime < departureTime < arrivalTime — and route integrity — departureAirport ≠ arrivalAirport. A flight may be published only once, and before publishing, the flight's openForBooking status must be false. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
2.Create a booking for passengers on a flight. A customer selects a specific open flight and supplies a list of passengers names. The system checks that there are no duplicate passengers on the flight and the current time is before the flight departure time. It then generates a booking for the customer and creates a reservation with a unique ID for each passenger in that booking. Each reservation is initially placed in "pending" status until the customer confirms it. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
3.Confirm or cancel an existing reservation in a booking. The system checks that the flight has not yet departed and is still open for booking. The customer can then confirm or cancel a reservation by providing its reservation ID. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
4.Close an open flight. An airline can close an existing flight that has not yet departed. The system verifies that the flight is currently open; if so, it changes the status to closed and cancels every confirmed reservation. Closing is not allowed on the same calendar day as the flight's departure — even if the current time is before the departure time. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
5.Retrieve all confirmed reservations for a specific flight. Given a flight object, the system retrieves every confirmed reservation on that flight, provided the flight is currently open for booking. It returns a list of reservations, or empty list if none exist.
```

# Class Diagram
```plantuml
@startuml

title flights Model

class Airline {
    flights : List<Flight>
    addFlight(f : Flight) : void
    closeFlight(flightId : String, now : EDate) : boolean
    publishFlight(f : Flight, now : EDate) : boolean
    removeFlight(f : Flight) : void
    searchFlights(origin : String, dest : String, date : EDate) : List<Flight>
}
class Airport {
    id : String
    servesForCities : List<City>
    addCity(c : City) : void
}
class Booking {
    customer : Customer
    reservations : List<Reservation>
    createReservation(f : Flight, passenger : String, now : EDate) : boolean
}
class City {
}
class Customer {
    bookings : List<Booking>
    addBooking(f : Flight, now : EDate, listOfPassengerNames : List<String>) : boolean
    cancel(reservationID : String, now : EDate) : boolean
    confirm(reservationID : String, now : EDate) : boolean
}
class Flight {
    arrivalTime : EDate
    departureTime : EDate
    id : String
    openForBooking : boolean
    arrivalAirport : Airport
    departureAirport : Airport
    reservations : List<Reservation>
    stopovers : List<Stopover>
    addStopover(stop : Stopover, now : EDate) : boolean
    getConfirmedReservations() : List<Reservation>
    removeStopover(stop : Stopover, now : EDate) : boolean
}
class Passenger {
    name : String
}
class Reservation {
    id : String
    status : ReservationStatus
    flight : Flight
    passenger : Passenger
}
class Stopover {
    arrivalTime : EDate
    departureTime : EDate
    airport : Airport
}
enum ReservationStatus {
    PENDING
    CONFIRMED
    CANCELED
}

Airline *-- "*" Flight : flights
Airport --> "*" City : servesForCities
Booking --> Customer : customer
Booking *-- "*" Reservation : reservations
Customer --> "*" Booking : bookings
Flight --> Airport : arrivalAirport
Flight --> Airport : departureAirport
Flight --> "*" Reservation : reservations
Flight *-- "*" Stopover : stopovers
Reservation --> Flight : flight
Reservation --> Passenger : passenger
Stopover --> Airport : airport
@enduml
```

2.Create a booking for passengers on a flight. A customer selects a specific open flight and supplies a list of passengers names. The system checks that there are no duplicate passengers on the flight and the current time is before the flight departure time. It then generates a booking for the customer and creates a reservation with a unique ID for each passenger in that booking. Each reservation is initially placed in "pending" status until the customer confirms it. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
3.Confirm or cancel an existing reservation in a booking. The system checks that the flight has not yet departed and is still open for booking. The customer can then confirm or cancel a reservation by providing its reservation ID. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
4.Close an open flight. An airline can close an existing flight that has not yet departed. The system verifies that the flight is currently open; if so, it changes the status to closed and cancels every confirmed reservation. Closing is not allowed on the same calendar day as the flight's departure — even if the current time is before the departure time. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
5.Retrieve all confirmed reservations for a specific flight. Given a flight object, the system retrieves every confirmed reservation on that flight, provided the flight is currently open for booking. It returns a list of reservations, or empty list if none exist.
```

# Requirement
```text
Airlines offer different flights. Each flight has its unique id. A flight is open for booking and closed by order of the company. A customer can book one or more flights, for different passengers. A reservation concerns a single flight and a single passenger, has a unique id. A reservation can be confirmed or canceled. A flight has a departure airport and an arrival airport. Each airport has its unique id. A flight has a day and time of departure, and a day and time of arrival (e.g. 2024-12-08 13:00:00). A flight may include stopovers in one or more airport(s). A stopover has a departure time and an arrival time. Each airport serves one or more cities.
Functional requirement:
1.Publish a flight for booking. An airline can publish a newly created flight to make it available for customer bookings. The system first confirms that the flight has valid departure and arrival timestamps in yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss format, then checks temporal consistency — currentTime < departureTime < arrivalTime — and route integrity — departureAirport ≠ arrivalAirport. A flight may be published only once, and before publishing, the flight's openForBooking status must be false. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
2.Create a booking for passengers on a flight. A customer selects a specific open flight and supplies a list of passengers names. The system checks that there are no duplicate passengers on the flight and the current time is before the flight departure time. It then generates a booking for the customer and creates a reservation with a unique ID for each passenger in that booking. Each reservation is initially placed in "pending" status until the customer confirms it. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
3.Confirm or cancel an existing reservation in a booking. The system checks that the flight has not yet departed and is still open for booking. The customer can then confirm or cancel a reservation by providing its reservation ID. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
4.Close an open flight. An airline can close an existing flight that has not yet departed. The system verifies that the flight is currently open; if so, it changes the status to closed and cancels every confirmed reservation. Closing is not allowed on the same calendar day as the flight's departure — even if the current time is before the departure time. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
5.Retrieve all confirmed reservations for a specific flight. Given a flight object, the system retrieves every confirmed reservation on that flight, provided the flight is currently open for booking. It returns a list of reservations, or empty list if none exist.
```

# Operation Specifications
Airline::addFlight
Summary: Adds a newly created flight to the airline's flight roster.
Algorithm: 
  1. Validate that f is not null.
  2. Verify that f does not already exist in the flights list (by id).
  3. Append f to the flights list.
  4. Return normally (void).
Related Features: flights
Related Classes: None
Input: f (Flight) - The newly instantiated flight object to be registered with the airline.
Output: None
Pre-condition: f is not null; f.id is unique among existing flights in this airline.
Post-condition: f is included in this.flights; the airline's inventory reflects the new flight.

Airline::publishFlight
Summary: Publishes a flight for customer booking after comprehensive validation.
Algorithm:
  1. Validate f.departureTime and f.arrivalTime match yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss format. If invalid, return false.
  2. Verify now < f.departureTime < f.arrivalTime. If invalid, return false.
  3. Verify f.departureAirport != f.arrivalAirport. If identical, return false.
  4. Verify f.openForBooking == false (ensures one-time publication rule). If true, return false.
  5. Set f.openForBooking = true.
  6. Return true.
Related Features: departureTime, arrivalTime, departureAirport, arrivalAirport, openForBooking
Related Classes: Airport
Input: f (Flight) - The flight object to publish; now (EDate) - Current system timestamp.
Output: boolean - true if successfully published, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: f is not null; timestamps are valid and chronologically correct; airports differ; flight is not already open for booking.
Post-condition: f.openForBooking becomes true; flight becomes visible and bookable by customers.

Airline::closeFlight
Summary: Closes an open flight, blocking further bookings and canceling all confirmed reservations.
Algorithm:
  1. Locate the flight f where f.id equals flightId. If not found, return false.
  2. Verify f.openForBooking is true. If false, return false.
  3. Verify now < f.departureTime. If not, return false.
  4. Verify calendar_date(now) != calendar_date(f.departureTime). If equal, return false.
  5. Set f.openForBooking = false.
  6. For each reservation r in f.reservations: if r.status == CONFIRMED, set r.status = CANCELED.
  7. Return true.
Related Features: id, openForBooking, departureTime, reservations
Related Classes: Reservation, ReservationStatus
Input: flightId (String) - Unique identifier of the flight to close; now (EDate) - Current system timestamp.
Output: boolean - true if successfully closed, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: Flight exists; currently open for booking; current time is strictly before departure; current calendar day differs from departure calendar day.
Post-condition: Flight's openForBooking becomes false; all confirmed reservations on the flight are changed to canceled.

Airline::removeFlight
Summary: Removes a flight from the airline's operational database.
Algorithm:
  1. Locate f in the flights list.
  2. Remove f from the list.
  3. Optionally clear external references if garbage collection isn't automatic.
  4. Return normally.
Related Features: flights
Related Classes: None
Input: f (Flight) - The flight instance to be removed.
Output: None
Pre-condition: f exists in this.flights; flight is not actively processing bookings (business policy inference).
Post-condition: f is permanently removed from this.flights; airline no longer schedules this flight.

Airline::searchFlights
Summary: Retrieves flights matching specified origin, destination, and departure date.
Algorithm:
  1. Initialize empty result list.
  2. For each flight f in flights:
     a. Check if f.departureAirport.servesForCities contains origin OR f.departureAirport.id matches origin.
     b. Check if f.arrivalAirport.servesForCities contains dest OR f.arrivalAirport.id matches dest.
     c. Check if calendar_date(f.departureTime) equals calendar_date(date).
     d. If all match, add f to result.
  3. Return result list.
Related Features: flights, departureAirport, arrivalAirport, departureTime
Related Classes: Airport, City
Input: origin (String) - Departure city/airport identifier; dest (String) - Arrival city/airport identifier; date (EDate) - Target travel date.
Output: List<Flight> - Matching flights sorted by departure time (inferred).
Pre-condition: Parameters are non-null; airline maintains valid airport-city mappings.
Post-condition: Returned list contains exactly those flights satisfying all three filter criteria.

# Requirement
```text
Airlines offer different flights. Each flight has its unique id. A flight is open for booking and closed by order of the company. A customer can book one or more flights, for different passengers. A reservation concerns a single flight and a single passenger, has a unique id. A reservation can be confirmed or canceled. A flight has a departure airport and an arrival airport. Each airport has its unique id. A flight has a day and time of departure, and a day and time of arrival (e.g. 2024-12-08 13:00:00). A flight may include stopovers in one or more airport(s). A stopover has a departure time and an arrival time. Each airport serves one or more cities.
Functional requirement:
1.Publish a flight for booking. An airline can publish a newly created flight to make it available for customer bookings. The system first confirms that the flight has valid departure and arrival timestamps in yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss format, then checks temporal consistency — currentTime < departureTime < arrivalTime — and route integrity — departureAirport ≠ arrivalAirport. A flight may be published only once, and before publishing, the flight's openForBooking status must be false. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
2.Create a booking for passengers on a flight. A customer selects a specific open flight and supplies a list of passengers names. The system checks that there are no duplicate passengers on the flight and the current time is before the flight departure time. It then generates a booking for the customer and creates a reservation with a unique ID for each passenger in that booking. Each reservation is initially placed in "pending" status until the customer confirms it. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
3.Confirm or cancel an existing reservation in a booking. The system checks that the flight has not yet departed and is still open for booking. The customer can then confirm or cancel a reservation by providing its reservation ID. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
4.Close an open flight. An airline can close an existing flight that has not yet departed. The system verifies that the flight is currently open; if so, it changes the status to closed and cancels every confirmed reservation. Closing is not allowed on the same calendar day as the flight's departure — even if the current time is before the departure time. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
5.Retrieve all confirmed reservations for a specific flight. Given a flight object, the system retrieves every confirmed reservation on that flight, provided the flight is currently open for booking. It returns a list of reservations, or empty list if none exist.
```

# Operation Specifications
Customer::confirm
Summary: Confirms a pending reservation belonging to the customer.
Algorithm:
  1. Search this.bookings and their reservations for reservationID. If not found, return false.
  2. Let r be the found reservation; let f be r.flight.
  3. Verify now < f.departureTime. If not, return false.
  4. Verify f.openForBooking == true. If false, return false.
  5. Set r.status = CONFIRMED.
  6. Return true.
Related Features: bookings, reservations, status
Related Classes: Reservation, ReservationStatus, Flight
Input: reservationID (String) - Unique ID of reservation to confirm; now (EDate) - Current timestamp.
Output: boolean - true if confirmation processed, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: Reservation belongs to this customer; flight hasn't departed; flight remains open for booking.
Post-condition: Reservation status transitions to CONFIRMED; booking becomes final and non-refundable (implied).

Customer::cancel
Summary: Cancels an existing reservation belonging to the customer.
Algorithm:
  1. Search this.bookings and their reservations for reservationID. If not found, return false.
  2. Let r be the found reservation; let f be r.flight.
  3. Verify now < f.departureTime. If not, return false.
  4. Verify f.openForBooking == true. If false, return false.
  5. Set r.status = CANCELED.
  6. Return true.
Related Features: bookings, reservations, status
Related Classes: Reservation, ReservationStatus, Flight
Input: reservationID (String) - Unique ID of reservation to cancel; now (EDate) - Current timestamp.
Output: boolean - true if cancellation processed, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: Reservation belongs to this customer; flight hasn't departed; flight remains open for booking.
Post-condition: Reservation status transitions to CANCELED; seat capacity is effectively released.

Customer::addBooking
Summary: Initiates a multi-passenger booking on a flight, creating individual pending reservations.
Algorithm:
  1. Validate listOfPassengerNames has no internal duplicates. If yes, return false.
  2. Verify no passenger in list already has a reservation on f. If yes, return false.
  3. Verify now < f.departureTime. If not, return false.
  4. Instantiate new Booking b; set b.customer = this; b.flight = f.
  5. For each name in listOfPassengerNames:
     a. Call b.createReservation(f, name, now).
     b. If any call returns false, delete b from customer.bookings, clear b.reservations, return false.
  6. Add b to this.bookings.
  7. Return true.
Related Features: bookings
Related Classes: Booking, Reservation, Passenger
Input: f (Flight) - Target flight; now (EDate) - Current timestamp; listOfPassengerNames (List<String>) - Names of passengers.
Output: boolean - true if entire booking batch succeeded, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: No duplicate names in input; no cross-duplicates with existing flight reservations; flight hasn't departed.
Post-condition: New Booking added to customer.bookings; all corresponding reservations are in PENDING state.

3. If there is any unspecified details, such as undefined constants, rates, and ratios, then you must infer them.
4. Make sure that all requirements can be covered.

# Requirement
```text
Airlines offer different flights. Each flight has its unique id. A flight is open for booking and closed by order of the company. A customer can book one or more flights, for different passengers. A reservation concerns a single flight and a single passenger, has a unique id. A reservation can be confirmed or canceled. A flight has a departure airport and an arrival airport. Each airport has its unique id. A flight has a day and time of departure, and a day and time of arrival (e.g. 2024-12-08 13:00:00). A flight may include stopovers in one or more airport(s). A stopover has a departure time and an arrival time. Each airport serves one or more cities.
Functional requirement:
1.Publish a flight for booking. An airline can publish a newly created flight to make it available for customer bookings. The system first confirms that the flight has valid departure and arrival timestamps in yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss format, then checks temporal consistency — currentTime < departureTime < arrivalTime — and route integrity — departureAirport ≠ arrivalAirport. A flight may be published only once, and before publishing, the flight's openForBooking status must be false. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
2.Create a booking for passengers on a flight. A customer selects a specific open flight and supplies a list of passengers names. The system checks that there are no duplicate passengers on the flight and the current time is before the flight departure time. It then generates a booking for the customer and creates a reservation with a unique ID for each passenger in that booking. Each reservation is initially placed in "pending" status until the customer confirms it. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
3.Confirm or cancel an existing reservation in a booking. The system checks that the flight has not yet departed and is still open for booking. The customer can then confirm or cancel a reservation by providing its reservation ID. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
4.Close an open flight. An airline can close an existing flight that has not yet departed. The system verifies that the flight is currently open; if so, it changes the status to closed and cancels every confirmed reservation. Closing is not allowed on the same calendar day as the flight's departure — even if the current time is before the departure time. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
5.Retrieve all confirmed reservations for a specific flight. Given a flight object, the system retrieves every confirmed reservation on that flight, provided the flight is currently open for booking. It returns a list of reservations, or empty list if none exist.
```

5.Retrieve all confirmed reservations for a specific flight. Given a flight object, the system retrieves every confirmed reservation on that flight, provided the flight is currently open for booking. It returns a list of reservations, or empty list if none exist.
```

# Requirement
```text
Airlines offer different flights. Each flight has its unique id. A flight is open for booking and closed by order of the company. A customer can book one or more flights, for different passengers. A reservation concerns a single flight and a single passenger, has a unique id. A reservation can be confirmed or canceled. A flight has a departure airport and an arrival airport. Each airport has its unique id. A flight has a day and time of departure, and a day and time of arrival (e.g. 2024-12-08 13:00:00). A flight may include stopovers in one or more airport(s). A stopover has a departure time and an arrival time. Each airport serves one or more cities.
Functional requirement:
1.Publish a flight for booking. An airline can publish a newly created flight to make it available for customer bookings. The system first confirms that the flight has valid departure and arrival timestamps in yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss format, then checks temporal consistency — currentTime < departureTime < arrivalTime — and route integrity — departureAirport ≠ arrivalAirport. A flight may be published only once, and before publishing, the flight's openForBooking status must be false. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
2.Create a booking for passengers on a flight. A customer selects a specific open flight and supplies a list of passengers names. The system checks that there are no duplicate passengers on the flight and the current time is before the flight departure time. It then generates a booking for the customer and creates a reservation with a unique ID for each passenger in that booking. Each reservation is initially placed in "pending" status until the customer confirms it. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
3.Confirm or cancel an existing reservation in a booking. The system checks that the flight has not yet departed and is still open for booking. The customer can then confirm or cancel a reservation by providing its reservation ID. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
4.Close an open flight. An airline can close an existing flight that has not yet departed. The system verifies that the flight is currently open; if so, it changes the status to closed and cancels every confirmed reservation. Closing is not allowed on the same calendar day as the flight's departure — even if the current time is before the departure time. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
5.Retrieve all confirmed reservations for a specific flight. Given a flight object, the system retrieves every confirmed reservation on that flight, provided the flight is currently open for booking. It returns a list of reservations, or empty list if none exist.
```

# Operation Specifications
Airline::addFlight
Summary: Adds a newly created flight to the airline's inventory, initializing it with a closed booking status.
Algorithm: 
  1. Verify that f.id does not already exist in the flights list.
  2. If valid, append f to flights.
  3. Set f.openForBooking to false.
  4. Return void.
Related Features: flights, Flight.id, Flight.openForBooking
Related Classes: Flight
Input: f (Flight): Flight object to be added. Must contain a valid unique id.
Output: void
Pre-condition: f.id is not present in Airline.flights.
Post-condition: f is contained in Airline.flights, and f.openForBooking is set to false.

Airline::publishFlight
Summary: Publishes a newly created flight for customer bookings after validating temporal and route constraints.
Algorithm: 
  1. Verify f.openForBooking == false. Return false if true.
  2. Parse f.departureTime and f.arrivalTime. Verify format is yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss. Return false if invalid.
  3. Verify now < f.departureTime < f.arrivalTime. Return false if violated.
  4. Verify f.departureAirport != f.arrivalAirport. Return false if violated.
  5. Set f.openForBooking = true.
  6. Add f to flights list if not already present.
  7. Return true.
Related Features: openForBooking, departureTime, arrivalTime, departureAirport, arrivalAirport, flights
Related Classes: Flight, Airport, EDate
Input: f (Flight): Flight object to publish. now (EDate): Current system timestamp.
Output: boolean: true if published successfully; false otherwise.
Pre-condition: Flight is not yet published, timestamps are valid and correctly ordered relative to now, departure and arrival airports differ.
Post-condition: Flight openForBooking is true, and flight is available in the airline's active list.

Airline::closeFlight
Summary: Closes an open flight and cancels all its confirmed reservations, subject to temporal constraints.
Algorithm: 
  1. Locate flight by flightId. Return false if not found.
  2. Verify f.openForBooking == true. Return false if false.
  3. Verify now < f.departureTime. Return false if not.
  4. Verify date(now) != date(f.departureTime). Return false if equal.
  5. Set f.openForBooking = false.
  6. For each r in f.reservations: if r.status == CONFIRMED, set r.status = CANCELED.
  7. Return true.
Related Features: openForBooking, departureTime, reservations, Reservation.status
Related Classes: Flight, Reservation, EDate
Input: flightId (String): Unique identifier of the flight. now (EDate): Current system timestamp.
Output: boolean: true if successfully closed and reservations cancelled; false otherwise.
Pre-condition: Flight exists, openForBooking is true, current time is before departure time, and current calendar day differs from departure calendar day.
Post-condition: Flight openForBooking is false, and all previously CONFIRMED reservations are changed to CANCELED.

Airline::removeFlight
Summary: Removes a flight from the airline's inventory.
Algorithm: 
  1. Search for f in flights list.
  2. If found, remove f from the list.
  3. Return void.
Related Features: flights
Related Classes: Flight
Input: f (Flight): Flight object to be removed.
Output: void
Pre-condition: f exists in Airline.flights.
Post-condition: f is removed from Airline.flights.

Airline::searchFlights
Summary: Retrieves flights matching specified origin, destination, and travel date.
Algorithm: 
  1. Initialize empty result list.
  2. For each f in flights:
     a. Check if f.departureAirport serves a city named origin.
     b. Check if f.arrivalAirport serves a city named dest.
     c. Check if date(f.departureTime) == date(date).
     d. If all match, add f to result list.
  3. Return result list.
Related Features: departureAirport, arrivalAirport, departureTime, flights
Related Classes: Airport, City, Flight, EDate
Input: origin (String): Name of departure city. dest (String): Name of arrival city. date (EDate): Target travel date.
Output: List<Flight>: Matching flights, or empty list if none.
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: Returns subset of flights satisfying geographic and temporal filters.

# Requirement
```text
Airlines offer different flights. Each flight has its unique id. A flight is open for booking and closed by order of the company. A customer can book one or more flights, for different passengers. A reservation concerns a single flight and a single passenger, has a unique id. A reservation can be confirmed or canceled. A flight has a departure airport and an arrival airport. Each airport has its unique id. A flight has a day and time of departure, and a day and time of arrival (e.g. 2024-12-08 13:00:00). A flight may include stopovers in one or more airport(s). A stopover has a departure time and an arrival time. Each airport serves one or more cities.
Functional requirement:
1.Publish a flight for booking. An airline can publish a newly created flight to make it available for customer bookings. The system first confirms that the flight has valid departure and arrival timestamps in yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss format, then checks temporal consistency — currentTime < departureTime < arrivalTime — and route integrity — departureAirport ≠ arrivalAirport. A flight may be published only once, and before publishing, the flight's openForBooking status must be false. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
2.Create a booking for passengers on a flight. A customer selects a specific open flight and supplies a list of passengers names. The system checks that there are no duplicate passengers on the flight and the current time is before the flight departure time. It then generates a booking for the customer and creates a reservation with a unique ID for each passenger in that booking. Each reservation is initially placed in "pending" status until the customer confirms it. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
3.Confirm or cancel an existing reservation in a booking. The system checks that the flight has not yet departed and is still open for booking. The customer can then confirm or cancel a reservation by providing its reservation ID. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
4.Close an open flight. An airline can close an existing flight that has not yet departed. The system verifies that the flight is currently open; if so, it changes the status to closed and cancels every confirmed reservation. Closing is not allowed on the same calendar day as the flight's departure — even if the current time is before the departure time. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
5.Retrieve all confirmed reservations for a specific flight. Given a flight object, the system retrieves every confirmed reservation on that flight, provided the flight is currently open for booking. It returns a list of reservations, or empty list if none exist.
```

# Operation Specifications
Customer::confirm
Summary: Confirms an existing pending reservation.
Algorithm: 
  1. Locate reservation r by reservationID. Return false if not found.
  2. Verify r.status == PENDING. Return false if not.
  3. Verify r.flight.openForBooking == true. Return false if false.
  4. Verify now < r.flight.departureTime. Return false if not.
  5. Set r.status = CONFIRMED.
  6. Return true.
Related Features: status, flight, Reservation.status, Flight.openForBooking, Flight.departureTime
Related Classes: Customer, Reservation, Flight, EDate
Input: reservationID (String): ID of the reservation to confirm. now (EDate): Current system timestamp.
Output: boolean: true if confirmed successfully; false otherwise.
Pre-condition: Reservation exists and is PENDING, flight is open for booking, current time is before flight departure.
Post-condition: Reservation status is updated to CONFIRMED.

Customer::cancel
Summary: Cancels an existing reservation.
Algorithm: 
  1. Locate reservation r by reservationID. Return false if not found.
  2. Verify r.status == PENDING or r.status == CONFIRMED. Return false if CANCELED.
  3. Verify r.flight.openForBooking == true. Return false if false.
  4. Verify now < r.flight.departureTime. Return false if not.
  5. Set r.status = CANCELED.
  6. Return true.
Related Features: status, flight, Reservation.status, Flight.openForBooking, Flight.departureTime
Related Classes: Customer, Reservation, Flight, EDate
Input: reservationID (String): ID of the reservation to cancel. now (EDate): Current system timestamp.
Output: boolean: true if cancelled successfully; false otherwise.
Pre-condition: Reservation exists (PENDING or CONFIRMED), flight is open for booking, current time is before flight departure.
Post-condition: Reservation status is updated to CANCELED.

Customer::addBooking
Summary: Creates a booking for selected passengers on an open flight.
Algorithm: 
  1. Verify f.openForBooking == true. Return false if false.
  2. Verify now < f.departureTime. Return false if not.
  3. Check for duplicate passenger names within listOfPassengerNames. Return false if duplicates exist.
  4. Check for duplicate passenger names across existing reservations on flight f. Return false if conflicts exist.
  5. Create a new Booking object associated with this Customer.
  6. For each passengerName in listOfPassengerNames:
     a. Generate a unique reservationID.
     b. Create a new Reservation object. Set reservation.id = reservationID, reservation.flight = f, reservation.passenger.name = passengerName, reservation.status = PENDING.
     c. Add reservation to Booking.reservations and Flight.reservations.
  7. Add Booking to Customer.bookings.
  8. Return true.
Related Features: openForBooking, departureTime, reservations, Reservation.id, Reservation.status, Booking.reservations
Related Classes: Customer, Flight, Booking, Reservation, Passenger, EDate
Input: f (Flight): Selected open flight. now (EDate): Current system timestamp. listOfPassengerNames (List<String>): Names of passengers.
Output: boolean: true if booking created successfully; false otherwise.
Pre-condition: Flight is open for booking, current time is before departure, passenger names are unique internally and do not conflict with existing reservations on the flight.
Post-condition: A new Booking is created containing multiple Reservations in PENDING status, linked to the flight and customer.

# Requirement
```text
Airlines offer different flights. Each flight has its unique id. A flight is open for booking and closed by order of the company. A customer can book one or more flights, for different passengers. A reservation concerns a single flight and a single passenger, has a unique id. A reservation can be confirmed or canceled. A flight has a departure airport and an arrival airport. Each airport has its unique id. A flight has a day and time of departure, and a day and time of arrival (e.g. 2024-12-08 13:00:00). A flight may include stopovers in one or more airport(s). A stopover has a departure time and an arrival time. Each airport serves one or more cities.
Functional requirement:
1.Publish a flight for booking. An airline can publish a newly created flight to make it available for customer bookings. The system first confirms that the flight has valid departure and arrival timestamps in yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss format, then checks temporal consistency — currentTime < departureTime < arrivalTime — and route integrity — departureAirport ≠ arrivalAirport. A flight may be published only once, and before publishing, the flight's openForBooking status must be false. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
2.Create a booking for passengers on a flight. A customer selects a specific open flight and supplies a list of passengers names. The system checks that there are no duplicate passengers on the flight and the current time is before the flight departure time. It then generates a booking for the customer and creates a reservation with a unique ID for each passenger in that booking. Each reservation is initially placed in "pending" status until the customer confirms it. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
3.Confirm or cancel an existing reservation in a booking. The system checks that the flight has not yet departed and is still open for booking. The customer can then confirm or cancel a reservation by providing its reservation ID. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
4.Close an open flight. An airline can close an existing flight that has not yet departed. The system verifies that the flight is currently open; if so, it changes the status to closed and cancels every confirmed reservation. Closing is not allowed on the same calendar day as the flight's departure — even if the current time is before the departure time. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
5.Retrieve all confirmed reservations for a specific flight. Given a flight object, the system retrieves every confirmed reservation on that flight, provided the flight is currently open for booking. It returns a list of reservations, or empty list if none exist.
```

title flights Model

class Airline {
    flights : List<Flight>
    addFlight(f : Flight) : void
    closeFlight(flightId : String, now : EDate) : boolean

    searchFlights(origin : String, dest : String, date : EDate) : List<Flight>

}

    bookings : List<Booking>

    cancel(reservationID : String, now : EDate) : boolean
    confirm(reservationID : String, now : EDate) : boolean
}

    arrivalTime : EDate
    departureTime : EDate
    id : String
    openForBooking : boolean
    arrivalAirport : Airport

    name : String
}

    id : String

}

    arrivalTime : EDate
    departureTime : EDate

    PENDING
    CONFIRMED
    CANCELED
}

Flight --> Airport : arrivalAirport

Reservation --> Flight : flight

Stopover --> Airport : airport
@enduml

# Operation Specifications
Flight::removeStopover
Summary: Removes a stopover from the flight's itinerary.
Algorithm: 
  1. Search for stop in stopovers list.
  2. If found, remove it from the list.
  3. Return true if removed, false otherwise.
Related Features: stopovers
Related Classes: Stopover, EDate
Input: stop (Stopover): Stopover object to remove. now (EDate): Current timestamp.
Output: boolean: true if successfully removed; false otherwise.
Pre-condition: stop exists in Flight.stopovers.
Post-condition: stop is removed from Flight.stopovers.

Flight::addStopover
Summary: Appends a stopover to the flight's itinerary.
Algorithm: 
  1. Verify stop is not already in stopovers.
  2. Append stop to stopovers.
  3. Return true.
Related Features: stopovers
Related Classes: Stopover, EDate
Input: stop (Stopover): Stopover object to add. now (EDate): Current timestamp (for logging/validation if needed).
Output: boolean: true if added; false otherwise.
Pre-condition: stop is not already present in Flight.stopovers.
Post-condition: stop is appended to Flight.stopovers.

Flight::getConfirmedReservations
Summary: Retrieves all confirmed reservations for this flight.
Algorithm: 
  1. Verify this.openForBooking == true. Return empty list if false.
  2. Initialize empty result list.
  3. For each r in this.reservations:
     a. If r.status == CONFIRMED, add r to result list.
  4. Return result list.
Related Features: openForBooking, reservations, Reservation.status
Related Classes: Flight, Reservation
Input: None.
Output: List<Reservation>: List of confirmed reservations, or empty list if none.
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: Returns subset of reservations where status is CONFIRMED, only accessible if flight is open for booking.

# Operation Specifications
Booking::createReservation
Summary: Creates a single pending reservation for a passenger on a flight within a booking context.
Algorithm: 
  1. Verify f.openForBooking == true. Return false if not.
  2. Check existing reservations on f for passenger name. Return false if duplicate found.
  3. Verify now < f.departureTime. Return false if not.
  4. Generate unique reservation ID.
  5. Instantiate Reservation with generated ID, status=PENDING, linked to f and passenger.
  6. Add reservation to this.reservations and f.reservations.
  7. Return true.
Related Features: reservations, Flight.reservations, Flight.openForBooking, Flight.departureTime, Reservation.id, Reservation.status, Passenger.name
Related Classes: Flight, Reservation, Passenger, EDate
Input: f (Flight): Target flight. passenger (String): Passenger name. now (EDate): Current timestamp.
Output: boolean: true if reservation created; false otherwise.
Pre-condition: Flight is open, passenger not already booked on flight, current time precedes departure.
Post-condition: New reservation created with PENDING status, attached to booking and flight.

5.Retrieve all confirmed reservations for a specific flight. Given a flight object, the system retrieves every confirmed reservation on that flight, provided the flight is currently open for booking. It returns a list of reservations, or empty list if none exist.
```

# Operation Specifications
Booking::createReservation
Summary: Creates a single pending reservation for a passenger on a flight within a booking context.
Algorithm: 
  1. Verify f.openForBooking == true. Return false if not.
  2. Check existing reservations on f for passenger name. Return false if duplicate found.
  3. Verify now < f.departureTime. Return false if not.
  4. Generate unique reservation ID.
  5. Instantiate Reservation with generated ID, status=PENDING, linked to f and passenger.
  6. Add reservation to this.reservations and f.reservations.
  7. Return true.
Related Features: reservations, Flight.reservations, Flight.openForBooking, Flight.departureTime, Reservation.id, Reservation.status, Passenger.name
Related Classes: Flight, Reservation, Passenger, EDate
Input: f (Flight): Target flight. passenger (String): Passenger name. now (EDate): Current timestamp.
Output: boolean: true if reservation created; false otherwise.
Pre-condition: Flight is open, passenger not already booked on flight, current time precedes departure.
Post-condition: New reservation created with PENDING status, attached to booking and flight.

    calTarget.setTime(date);
    
    for (Flight f : this.getFlights()) {
      boolean depMatch = false;
      Airport depAirport = f.getDepartureAirport();
      if (depAirport != null) {
        for (City c : depAirport.getServesForCities()) {
          if (c.getName() != null && c.getName().equals(origin)) {
            depMatch = true;
            break;
          }
        }
      }
      
      boolean arrMatch = false;
      Airport arrAirport = f.getArrivalAirport();
      if (arrAirport != null) {
        for (City c : arrAirport.getServesForCities()) {
          if (c.getName() != null && c.getName().equals(dest)) {
            arrMatch = true;
            break;
          }
        }
      }
      
      boolean timeMatch = false;
      if (f.getDepartureTime() != null) {
        Calendar calDep = Calendar.getInstance();
        calDep.setTime(f.getDepartureTime());
        if (calTarget.get(Calendar.YEAR) == calDep.get(Calendar.YEAR) &&
            calTarget.get(Calendar.MONTH) == calDep.get(Calendar.MONTH) &&
            calTarget.get(Calendar.DAY_OF_MONTH) == calDep.get(Calendar.DAY_OF_MONTH)) {
          timeMatch = true;
        }
      }
      
      if (depMatch && arrMatch && timeMatch) {
        result.add(f);
      }
    }
    return result;
  }

   * Summary: Creates a single pending reservation for a passenger on a flight within a booking context.
   * Algorithm: 
   * Related Features: Booking.reservations, Flight.reservations, Flight.openForBooking, Flight.departureTime, Reservation.id, Reservation.status, Passenger.name
   * Related Classes: Flight, Reservation, Passenger
   * Input: f (Flight): Target flight. passenger (Passenger): Passenger object representing the booker. now (EDate): Current timestamp.
   * Output: boolean: true if reservation successfully created; false otherwise.
   * Pre-condition: Flight is open for booking, passenger is not already booked on the flight, and current time is strictly before the flight's departure time.
   * Post-condition: A new Reservation instance with PENDING status is created and added to both the booking's and the flight's reservation lists.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public boolean createReservation(final Flight f, final String passenger, final Date now)
  {
    // Pre-condition: Flight is open for booking
    if (!f.isOpenForBooking()) {
      return false;
    }
    // Pre-condition: current time is strictly before the flight's departure time
    if (!now.before(f.getDepartureTime())) {
      return false;
    }
    // Pre-condition: passenger is not already booked on the flight
    for (Reservation existingRes : f.getReservations()) {
      if (passenger.equals(existingRes.getName())) {
        return false;
      }
    }

    // Post-condition: Create new reservation instance with PENDING status
    Reservation newRes = FlightsFactory.eINSTANCE.createReservation();
    newRes.setName(passenger);
    newRes.setStatus(Reservation.Status.PENDING);

    // Add reservation to both booking's and flight's lists
    this.getReservations().add(newRes);
    f.getReservations().add(newRes);

    return true;
  }

  public boolean createReservation(final Flight f, final String passenger, final Date now)
  {
    // Pre-condition: Flight is open for booking
    if (!f.isOpenForBooking()) {
      return false;
    }
    // Pre-condition: current time is strictly before the flight's departure time
    if (!now.before(f.getDepartureTime())) {
      return false;
    }
    // Pre-condition: passenger is not already booked on the flight
    for (Reservation existingRes : f.getReservations()) {
      if (passenger.equals(existingRes.getName())) {
        return false;

    Reservation newRes = FlightsFactory.eINSTANCE.createReservation();
    newRes.setName(passenger);
    newRes.setStatus(Reservation.Status.PENDING);

    // Add reservation to both booking's and flight's lists
    this.getReservations().add(newRes);
    f.getReservations().add(newRes);

    return true;
  }

      return false;

        return false;
      }

    Passenger newPassenger = FlightsFactory.eINSTANCE.createPassenger();
    newPassenger.setName(passenger);
    newRes.setPassenger(newPassenger);
    newRes.setStatus(ReservationStatus.PENDING);

    // Add reservation to both booking's and flight's lists
    this.getReservations().add(newRes);
    f.getReservations().add(newRes);

    return true;

    }
    
    if (targetRes.getStatus() == ReservationStatus.PENDING) {
      targetRes.setStatus(ReservationStatus.CONFIRMED);
      return true;
    }
    
    return false;
  }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Cancels an existing reservation.
   * Algorithm: 
   * Related Features: bookings, status, flight, openForBooking, departureTime
   * Related Classes: Booking, Reservation, Flight, EDate
   * Input: reservationID (String): ID of the reservation to cancel. now (EDate): Current system timestamp.
   * Output: boolean: true if cancelled successfully; false otherwise.
   * Pre-condition: Reservation exists and is in PENDING or CONFIRMED status, associated flight is open for booking, current time is before flight departure time.
   * Post-condition: Reservation status is updated to CANCELED.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public boolean cancel(final String reservationID, final Date now)
  {
    Reservation targetRes = null;
    for (Booking b : this.getBookings()) {
      for (Reservation r : b.getReservations()) {
        if (reservationID.equals(r.getReservationID())) {
          targetRes = r;
          break;
        }
      }
      if (targetRes != null) {
        break;
      }
    }
    
    if (targetRes == null) {
      return false;
    }
    
    Flight f = targetRes.getFlight();
    if (!f.isOpenForBooking() || !now.before(f.getDepartureTime())) {
      return false;
    }
    
    ReservationStatus status = targetRes.getStatus();
    if (status == ReservationStatus.PENDING || status == ReservationStatus.CONFIRMED) {
      targetRes.setStatus(ReservationStatus.CANCELED);
      return true;
    }
    
    return false;
  }

            arrMatch = true;
            break;
          }
        }
      }

          timeMatch = true;
        }
      }

        result.add(f);
      }
    }
    return result;

  1.1 Consider the related classes in the Javadocs.
  1.2 Locate these files in your project.
  1.3 Generate the class summarization.
2. Read the error messages carefully.
3. Do your best to fix the errors locally without introducing new types, fields, and methods.
4. You should not remove faulty methods to eliminate compilation errors.
5. Do not change parts without errors.

## EMF Coding Style
- When possible, call getter/setter methods to access field values. Do not read/write raw fields derived from the class diagram.
- The getter of a boolean attribute `bv` looks like `isBv()`, e.g., `isIsTrue()` for `isTrue`.
- When possibe, use the creation factory for object creation.
- To create an EList instance, import and use `org.eclipse.emf.common.util.BasicEList`.

        }
      }

        result.add(f);

   * Input: reservationID (String): ID of the reservation to cancel. now (EDate): Current system timestamp.
   * Output: boolean: true if cancelled successfully; false otherwise.
   * Pre-condition: Reservation exists and is in PENDING or CONFIRMED status, associated flight is open for booking, current time is before flight departure time.
   * Post-condition: Reservation status is updated to CANCELED.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public boolean cancel(final String reservationID, final Date now)
  {
    Reservation targetRes = null;
    for (Booking b : this.getBookings()) {
      for (Reservation r : b.getReservations()) {
        if (reservationID.equals(r.getReservationId())) {
          targetRes = r;
          break;
        }
      }
      if (targetRes != null) {
        break;
      }
    }
    
    if (targetRes == null) {
      return false;
    }
    
    Flight f = targetRes.getFlight();
    if (!f.isOpenForBooking() || !now.before(f.getDepartureTime())) {
      return false;
    }
    
    ReservationStatus status = targetRes.getStatus();
    if (status == ReservationStatus.PENDING || status == ReservationStatus.CONFIRMED) {
      targetRes.setStatus(ReservationStatus.CANCELED);
      return true;
    }
    
    return false;
  }
